answer: Sustained-attention audition.** Each identity must complete a randomized task stream and hold a decayed attention score above a mesa threshold before its votes are counted. The score drops continuously, so a farm must staff every identity with real agent-hours; idle accounts lose eligibility. A relic timestamp records each interaction, making replay detectable. The anchor rule ties voting weight to the lowest score in an identity's recent window, so burst attention cannot substitute for duration. An attacker pays sustained per-identity labor cost, not a one-time fee.
